questions.question: Dr. Sami receives a non-verbal patient with autism spectrum disorder. Dr. Mina advises him to use pictograms. Why are pictograms effective?
options: They offer predictable and reassuring visual communication
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Pictograms offer predictable visual communication that reduces anxiety.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will prepare pictograms for my practice.'

questions.question: Dr. Mina has a patient with severe attention deficit disorder. What strategy should she adopt to maintain attention?
options: Short sessions, regular breaks, and clear, short instructions
Very long sessions to exhaust them
Speak very quickly to stimulate them
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Patients with attention disorders need short and structured sessions.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will adapt the session duration.'

questions.question: Dr. Sami has a patient with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) who touches the doorknob several times before sitting down. Dr. Mina advises him to...
options: Respect their ritual and give them extra time
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'OCD patients' rituals are regulation mechanisms that should be respected.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will give them the necessary time.'

questions.question: Dr. Mina must treat a patient with cerebral palsy. What postural adaptation is necessary?
options: Use positioning cushions and wedges to stabilize the patient
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Adapted positioning is essential for patient comfort and safety.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will equip myself with positioning cushions.'

questions.question: Dr. Sami has a patient with severe social phobia. They refuse to make eye contact. Dr. Mina advises him to...
options: Not force eye contact and adapt communication
Ask them to look in the eyes
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Forcing eye contact can increase anxiety in patients with social phobia.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will respect their space.'

questions.question: Dr. Mina receives a patient with a severe eating disorder. What approach should she adopt?
options: A cautious approach, avoiding comments on weight or appearance
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Patients with eating disorders are sensitive to comments about the body.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will be careful with my words.'

questions.question: Dr. Sami has a patient with moderate intellectual disability. What is the best communication strategy?
options: Use simple sentences, concrete words, and visual aids
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Communication should be adapted to the patient's level of understanding.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will simplify my language.'

questions.question: Dr. Mina must treat a patient with severe dementia. What is the most appropriate approach?
options: A gentle, reassuring approach focused on the present
Constantly remind them of their illness
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Patients with dementia live in the present and need kindness.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will adopt a gentle and reassuring approach.'

questions.question: Dr. Sami has a patient with a strong fear of failure. Dr. Mina advises him to...
options: Set very small and achievable goals to create successes
Set impossible goals to motivate them
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Small successes reinforce the patient's confidence.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will divide the treatment plan into simple steps.'

questions.question: Dr. Mina receives a patient with borderline personality disorder. What is the golden rule with this type of patient?
options: Maintain clear boundaries and a consistent attitude
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Borderline patients need clear boundaries and consistency.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will establish clear rules with this patient.'

questions.question: Dr. Sami has a patient with a fear of swallowing. What strategy should he adopt?
options: Reassure about sensations, offer water before treatment, and take breaks
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Fear of swallowing requires reassurance and breaks.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will offer water before treatment.'

questions.question: Dr. Mina must treat a patient with severe agoraphobia. What adaptation is necessary?
options: Schedule the consultation early in the morning, with direct access and reduced staff
Make them wait in a crowded waiting room
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Agoraphobic patients need a low-stimulation environment.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will organize calm consultations for them.'

questions.question: Dr. Sami receives a patient with oral mutilation (e.g., scarring). Dr. Mina advises him to...
options: Approach the subject delicately, focusing on care and referring to a psychologist
Ask them for explanations about their scars
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Mutilations are signs of distress that should be approached delicately.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will focus on care and refer.'

questions.question: Dr. Mina has a patient with dyskinesia (involuntary movements). How to adapt treatment?
options: Use gentle restraint and stabilized positioning
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Gentle restraint and positioning secure the patient.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will use positioning wedges.'

questions.question: Dr. Sami has a patient with tetraplegia. What is the priority for welcoming them?
options: Ensure the accessibility of the practice (ramp, adapted chair, chair height)
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Accessibility is the basis of welcoming wheelchair patients.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will check the accessibility of my practice.'

questions.question: Dr. Mina receives a patient with profound deafness. What is the best communication solution?
options: A sign language interpreter or a subtitling system
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'A professional interpreter is the most suitable solution.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will offer an interpreter to my deaf patients.'

questions.question: Dr. Sami has a patient with prosopagnosia (difficulty recognizing faces). What adaptation is necessary?
options: Introduce yourself systematically and wear a visible badge
Show them a photo of themselves
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Systematic introduction is essential for patients with prosopagnosia.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will always introduce myself with my badge.'

questions.question: Dr. Mina must treat a patient with severe generalized anxiety. What is the most effective strategy?
options: A multimodal approach: relaxation, explanations, progressiveness, and psychotherapy
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Generalized anxiety requires a multimodal approach.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will offer relaxation sessions to this patient.'

questions.question: Dr. Sami has a patient with epilepsy. What safety measure should he take?
options: Know first aid procedures in case of a seizure and avoid triggers
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Dentists should know first aid procedures for epileptic patients.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will train in first aid procedures.'

questions.question: Dr. Mina receives a patient with anterograde memory disorder. What is the right strategy?
options: Repeat instructions at each visit and use written memory aids
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Repetition and memory aids are essential for these patients.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will give written instructions to this patient.'

questions.question: Dr. Sami has a patient with psychosis. What attitude should he adopt?
options: Stay calm, speak gently, and do not confront delusional ideas
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'We must not confront delusions, but stay calm and kind.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will stay calm and not discuss their ideas.'

questions.question: Dr. Mina receives a patient with a swallowing disorder. What precaution should she take?
options: Position the patient in a semi-seated position and avoid water splashes
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'The semi-seated position reduces the risk of aspiration.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will raise the backrest of the chair.'

questions.question: Dr. Sami has a patient with Tourette syndrome. How should he react to tics?
options: Ignore the tics and continue treatment normally
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Tics are involuntary. They should be ignored to avoid worsening them.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will ignore the tics and focus on treatment.'

questions.question: Dr. Mina must treat a patient with aortic valve stenosis. What special precaution is necessary?
options: Monitor blood pressure and avoid intense stress
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Stress can be dangerous for patients with aortic stenosis.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will monitor their blood pressure and reassure them.'

questions.question: Dr. Sami, after having managed complex cases of patients with specific needs with Dr. Mina, receives her congratulations. What is the next step for Dr. Sami?
options: Become an expert in helping relationships and care for vulnerable patients
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Mastery of care for vulnerable patients is a valuable skill. Becoming an expert is the next step.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will train in supporting vulnerable patients.'
